text:
incident-bot: PAGING: Multiple upstream peering sessions to CarrierZ (AS64570) in eu-west2 are flapping. Alerts: high packet loss, TCP retransmits, and elevated DNS timeouts observed. Impact: some EU customers seeing 5xxs and slow api.latency for 2+ regions.
Alex: oncall here, looking. assigning to Maria for network triage.
Maria: I'm on it, pulling BGP tables now.
Chen: grabbing logs from edge proxies + egress NATs to correlate.
Maria: seeing AS path prepend changes, a bunch of withdraws from peer-peer links. here's a quick BGP snippet:```bgp summary
Peer 10.10.20.1 AS64570 ESTAB 1d
Peer 10.10.21.1 AS64570 flaps 5x last 10m
Prefixes received: 120k -> 0 (intermittent)
```
Maria: traceroute from eu-west2-egress to 8.8.8.8 shows hops dropping in mid-transit: ```traceroute 8.8.8.8
 1 10.0.0.1 1.2 ms
 2 203.0.113.1 8.8 ms
 3 198.51.100.45 * * *
```
Jamal: affected services list? we saw increased 502 rate on /v1/generate and embedding ingestion queue backpressure.
Priya: support already fielding tickets from several customers in EU. escalation badge applied.
Support Lead: collecting impacted customers list from CS dashboard, prioritising enterprise tenants.
Alex: initial mitigation ideas: shift egress for eu-west2 to secondary transit (CarrierY) via policy override, and lower BGP local-pref for CarrierZ to prefer other peers. need network approval to change routes.
Maria: agreed. I'll open a temporary outbound policy to prefer CarrierY for prod egress in eu-west2. prepping ACL and route-map now.
Chen: if we shift egress, watch KV cache locality for LLM KV cache nodes — possible latency bump for some requests. add canary route first.
Maria: starting canary: applying route-map on two border routers (eu-west2-bdr-1/2) to prefer CarrierY for prefix set customers-prod.
netops-bot: deploybot: route-map update queued for eu-west2-bdr-1 at commit 2140001560.
Alex: runbook note: if canary shows >20% error reduction within 5 minutes we can promote. otherwise revert.
~5m later~
Maria: canary notes: 60% drop in packet loss on those nodes, DNS retries down to baseline.
Priya: ticket 9876: customer ACME reports reduced errors, confirming impact improvement.
Jamal: telemetry: /v1/generate 5xxs reduced from 8% -> 1.2% for EU traffic after canary. good sign.
Chen: deploying promotion on remaining bdrs now. will monitor KV cache misses.
netops-bot: deploybot: route-map promotion scheduled for eu-west2-bdr-3/4 at 2140002100.
Maria: provider contacted: CarrierZ case #CZ-44921 opened. they acknowledge internal maintenance; investigating.
Maria: they report a hardware flapping module causing mid-path packet drops, ETA for stable routes unknown.
Alex: OK, mitigation path is live. next: update status page, notify sales/CS SME for impacted enterprise, start RCA channel. Priya take communications?
Priya: drafting customer message: summary, mitigation steps, ETA pending provider, and offer to exec-summaries for enterprise.
Support Lead: pushing to enterprise dashboard and CCing legal for SLA implications.
Jamal: schedule handoff to night oncall: Chen will take next shift. include runbook steps: revert route-map, cookbook for AS-path adjustments, and provider ticket link.
Chen: copying mitigation commands into runbook now. snippet:```bash
# prefer CarrierY
set policy route-map PREFER-CARRY set local-preference 200
apply to interfaces: eu-west2-bdr-*
```
Alex: final check: any lingering DNS TTL anomalies or cache poisoning risks?
Maria: TTL spike during flap but now back to normal. no evidence of cache poisoning.
Priya: customer comms ready to send after legal review.
netops-bot: incident-bot note: incident severity remains Sev2 while provider in investigation and our mitigation active.
Support Lead: estimated impact window: 31 minutes (start 2140001234 -> mitigation promoted 2140002970).
Chen: handoff note: monitoring dashboards pinned, pager rotation updated, next oncall: Chen (overnight).
Alex: thanks team. keep provider ticket linked and update incident channel on any regression. closing out live mitigation phase.
incident-bot: Incident updated: mitigation applied, monitoring. Please ack if you have any remaining actions.
